About me

I make brands more interesting on the internet.

I’m a social media strategist who turns cultural moments into scroll-stopping content. I led Tripadvisor’s global rebrand, launched TikTok accounts at Mars, and spent years at agencies helping brands show up where people actually pay attention.

I’ve worked across travel, lifestyle, food, fashion, tech, beauty and fitness. Basically, if it exists online, I’ve made content about it.

The ask
Make Tripadvisor relevant to younger travelers, with social as the way in.
What I did
I led the strategy with our agency partner. We moved the feed away from one-off posts and toward travel programming people come back for. That meant a clear role for social, three content pillars, a job for every channel, a sharper Type C voice that flexes by platform, plus original editorial series, creators and community management.

Hotel Bookings Project

The ask
Our sales team wanted Gen Z’s attention and more hotel bookings, through three organic Instagram posts on Tripadvisor’s channels.
What I did
We found that Gen Z gravitates toward niche humor and unexpected twists, and built all three videos around that.
What happened
Over half a million organic views. The videos became cornerstone assets for Tripadvisor’s paid social hotel campaign on TikTok.
500K+organic views, then paid TikTok ads

Revamping Reviews

The ask
Show off Tripadvisor’s 1 billion reviews in a way that would stop the scroll.
What I did
I developed two breakout concepts: a static series of hilariously helpful travel tips, and “Speed Reviews,” videos of people racing through destinations while rattling off real reviews.
What happened
Thousands of views and high engagement. Proof that smart creative can turn data into entertainment.
1Breviews turned into scroll-stoppers

Hard Rock Cafe

The ask
Hard Rock Cafe’s 50+ accounts were posting inconsistent content that didn’t match the brand’s iconic voice or mission.
What I did
I built a scalable monthly content calendar and community management playbook for the U.S. and Europe, plus a custom hashtag strategy that got fans to tag their Hard Rock experiences.
What happened
Authentic fan content became a tool that boosted engagement, expanded reach and gave every cafe’s channels one cohesive story.
50+accounts, one voice

The program in action

The ask
Create an always-on influencer program that promoted booking experiences on Tripadvisor’s website.
What I did
I targeted micro-influencers in niche categories with high engagement, and used strategic briefs to guide who we picked and what they made. In July we launched the updated program with a sharper strategy and tighter creator briefing, then amplified the best content with paid media.
What happened
87 pieces of creator content in the first two months, across Tripadvisor and Viator. Genuine loyalty over vanity metrics.
87pieces of creator content in two months

Social-owned rapid response

The gap
Agency work runs on longer-term, longer-brief processes. Trends and timely moments needed a faster lane, owned by social.
What I built
A social-owned process with the creative team: a Social Squad of internal contributors with strong social instincts, Currents to spot timely trends and news, and weekly sprints that turn them into Tripadvisor and Viator memes and light video.
What happened
Internal creative became a strong complement to the agency’s video and creator-led work. The top posts: a product-feature meme, a brand-relevant meme and the Travelers’ Choice winners list.
Weeklysprints for trend work
36internal creative posts since Jan 2026

Tripadvisor Studio

The idea
One high-production hero show anchors our new TV model: The Travel Agency, hosted by our in-house creator. It’s structured but unscripted, set inside “the world’s first agency to help you reclaim your agency,” with refillable segments of reviews, UGC and street correspondents.
The set
A nostalgic-meets-Gen Z world built on three pillars: nostalgic, unserious and travel-centric. Three vignettes give every segment its own corner of the set.
The mix
Half of production in the studio to build the world, half outside to bring audiences the best experiences.
50/50in-studio and outside

Three vignettes, one cohesive set

The Desk

Home base for intros, transitions and solo segments, surrounded by accessible travel props.

On Tour With

A segment where we get up close and personal with the amazing tour guides from Tripadvisor’s bookable experiences.

The Interview Spot

A casual conversation zone for guests, guides and travelers.
